patronOf.en-US: Lay sister of St. Martha's, Milan
patronOf.pt-BR: Irmã conversa de Santa Marta, em Milão

prayerExcerpt.en-US: "I must work while I can, while I have time."
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: "Devo trabalhar enquanto posso, enquanto tenho tempo."

meta.face: A Lombard countrywoman of about fifty with a sun-weathered, ruddy complexion and a SHORT, BROAD face under a LOW, WIDE brow — high, round APPLE cheekbones, a short, broad nose with a slightly upturned tip, small, bright, deep-set dark-brown eyes under thick, straight dark brows, a wide mouth with thin lips set in a patient half-smile, a small, firm, square chin; hair hidden by the wimple; her gaze lifted a little, cheerful and willing.
meta.basis: No portrait from life; the nineteenth-century roundel on Wikipedia shows her in the black Augustinian habit, white wimple and black veil with an olive branch and bread, which the card keeps. The book tells of a peasant girl who worked the fields near Milan and, as a lay sister of St. Martha's, begged the community's food through the city; the sturdy, broad country face is our choice, kept apart from the set's oval-faced nuns (`rita_cascia`, `hedwig`).
